notes:
VERDICT: FAIL, and a NET REGRESSION against attempt 2. Attempt 2 scored min 93 with zero Critical and zero Major - it was waiver-eligible. Attempt 3 carries THREE MAJOR findings, all of them regressions against named locked features, so it is not waiver-eligible. If the retry budget is spent, ship candidate-2, not candidate-3.

THE OPTION STILL READS CORRECTLY. There is no Critical finding. The garment is unmistakably a flat front with exactly one short, tapered, stitched dart per front panel, each caught under a belt loop, terminating high on the hip, and clearly separated from the pressed leg crease. A customer comparing this against a pleated option would identify it correctly. Three of the four things attempt 2 was told to fix DID improve: the crease moved from 29-33% to 37-40% of leg width in from the outer edge (target 53%), the crease-to-dart-point lateral offset fell from 43px to 15px on the left, and the lighting imbalance fell from 3.81:1 to 2.73:1 at worst. The left dart's tilt is now essentially exact at 3.6 degrees against the drawing's 3.3.

WHAT WENT WRONG. The corrections were applied by re-shooting rather than by nudging, and three things that were already right came back wrong. (1) The waistband deepened from 72.0px to 82.5px at provably identical framing while the belt-loop pitch shrank from 368.7px to 354.7px, taking the pitch/depth landmark from 5.15 to 4.35 against the drawing's 5.55 - a 22% miss on the ratio the previous grade explicitly named as its normaliser. (2) The right belt loop and its dart both slid ~14px inboard while the left stayed put, so dart head offsets from centre front went from 189.0/192.0 (1.6% apart) to 195.5/175.0 (11.1% apart). (3) The left dart-to-crease gap shrank from 3.85 to 2.57 waistband-depths, below the locked 3.2-3.5 band, because the left dart grew 23px longer while the crease onset moved down only 21px. Separately, two attempt-2 corrections were simply not applied at all: the belt loops were not shortened (bar tack still 0.33 wb below the seam against the drawing's 0.21, and the dart head now sits even lower at 0.114 loop-pitches below the seam versus 0.072 last time), and the white shirt band with its button is still at the top of the frame, still the brightest object in the picture at luminance 253.

MEASUREMENT BASIS AND LANDMARK VALIDATION. No printed dimension callout exists anywhere on the illustration, so NO centimetre figure is recoverable for waistband depth, dart length, dart intake, belt loop pitch or crease position. Every number above is a pixel count or a ratio. I validated the framing FIRST rather than trusting a normaliser: the two renders' silhouettes are identical at y=70 (x137 to x752 in both) and within 1-2.5% of width at every sampled row to y=1150, so proportion changes between attempts are real and not zoom. Because the previous grade's own normaliser (loop pitch / waistband depth) turned out to be the thing that moved, I re-derived BOTH of its components in BOTH candidates with one method and cross-checked against a third scale, the waistband silhouette width. Drawing: waistband width 806px (x197-1003), depth 78.4px (top-edge centroid y=79.5, seam centroid y=158.25, confirmed by per-column reads of 77-80px across x=420-780), loop centres 382.5 and 817.5 from the y95-145 column runs, pitch 435px. Render depths were read per column as the bright-to-dark top edge minus the seam trough and taken as a median over 26 columns, excluding x=500 where the fly contaminates the trough.

TRAPS CHECKED, INCLUDING ONE I NEARLY FELL INTO. (a) I first read the contrast-stretched crops and concluded that the dart had merged into the crease into one unbroken line from waistband to hem - the exact candidate-1 failure. That was WRONG, and the contrast stretch caused it: the drape shading between the dart point and the crease head survives the stretch and reads as a continuous line to the eye. The amplitude trace disproves it - 5-10 grey levels in the gap against 20-29 in the dart and 20-38 in the crease. I would have failed a correct image on that. (b) Feature-identity: my first right-dart trace with a plus/minus-12px tracking window wandered off onto the inseam at x=580-600 by y=700; re-run with a fixed wide window over x=600-720 it found the real crease at x=642-676. (c) Sign/side: the left dart's dark peak sits outboard of its bright peak and the right dart's sits inboard, so a dark-only tracker gives dart offsets that are systematically wrong by half the ridge width and would have manufactured a false asymmetry. All symmetry figures use the dark/bright MIDPOINT, and that method reproduces the previous grade's candidate-2 numbers (189/192 head, 200/201 point) to within 1px, which is what gives me confidence the candidate-3 numbers (195.5/175.0) are a real change and not a method difference. (d) Span: the drawing's crease was re-verified as a contiguous 467-row run, y681 to y1147, not a partial mask. (e) Saturation: see below.

WHAT I COULD NOT MEASURE - DISCARDED READINGS. (1) THE SIDE POCKET INSET. The locked entry "opening set 0.53 waistband-depths inboard of the side seam" could not be verified either way and I am NOT calling it lost. An automated ridge search inboard of the silhouette edge saturated against its own window: it returned an inset of 12-17px in BOTH candidates and on both sides, pinned to the search window's inner bound of edge+12, which is the rolled silhouette edge and not a pocket. I discarded it rather than report it. Visual inspection of local-contrast-normalised crops does show a slanted opening on both sides of candidate-3, converging with the side seam by about y=400 (drawing: y=500), but it sits visibly closer to the side seam than candidate-2's and I cannot put a defensible number on it. (2) DART INTAKE - the width of cloth removed. The drawing's dart is a constant-width red annotation stroke (15, 17, 15, 19px down its length), so it carries no taper information; I can confirm the render's darts taper but cannot check intake against the drawing. (3) Any real-world dimension in centimetres, for the reason above. (4) A defensible absolute target for the pitch/depth ratio in a PHOTOGRAPH. A flat orthographic drawing and a photograph of a body do not share a projection: the loops sit on a curved front, so their projected separation is compressed relative to the flat sketch while the waistband depth is not, which inflates depth/pitch in any photo. A crude cylinder model puts the expected photographic ratio near 4.9 rather than 5.55, which would make candidate-2 (5.15) slightly over and candidate-3 (4.35) about 11% under rather than 22%. I have reported the raw ratio and flagged the caveat; the finding stands either way because the lock is stated as a ratio with a 0.9% tolerance and both the sign and the magnitude of the move are unambiguous. (5) Fabric drape, press quality and fibre rendering have no counterpart in a flat line drawing and were judged on tailoring plausibility only.

SCORING. All nine categories fall below the 98 bar. Six fall below the 95 waiver: symmetry 88, dimensions 89, geometry 90, placement 92, blueprint-match 92, composition 93. Because there are Major findings, the waiver route is closed regardless.

The only writes were contrast-stretched and local-contrast-normalised crops in the session scratchpad.
